<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par130 />{{GHGpar-heading|130|Wider Use of the Construct State}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|130|a}}
The construct state, which, according to {{GHGpar|89|a}}, primarily represents only the immediate government by one substantive of the following word (or combination of words), is frequently employed in rapid narrative as a connecting form, even apart from the genitive relation; so especially—

(1) Before prepositions,<ref>Cf. König, ‘Die Ueberwucherung des St.-constr.-Gebrauchs im Semit.,’ {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 53, 521 ff.</ref> particularly in elevated (prophetic or poetic) style, especially when the nomen regens is a participle. Thus before {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=שִׂמְחַת בַּקָּצִיר|translate=the joy in the harvest}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=9|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=1|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=136|verse=8}}f.; in participles, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=9|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=19|verse=8|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=84|verse=7}}, and especially often when {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} with a suffix follows the participle, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=2|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־חוֹסֵי בוֹ}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=1|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=8|verse=16}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=24|verse=1}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=64|verse=9}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=רֹאֶה}} should be read); 98:7.<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=8|verse=11}} the article is even used before a construct state followed by {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}}, in order to determine the whole combination {{GHGheb|text=שְׁכוּנֵי בָֽאֳהָלִים|translate=tent-dwellers}}, taken as one word; cf., however, the remarks in {{GHGpar|127|f}}–i on similar grammatical solecisms.</ref>—Before {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=9|verse=6}} (but read probably {{GHGheb|text=מַתֲמַדֵּי כַסְפָּם}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=58|verse=5}} (before {{GHGheb|text=לָמוֹ}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=18|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=2|verse=18}} (before {{GHGheb|text=לָךְ}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=6|verse=55}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=23|verse=28|hidebook=1}}; in participles, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=38|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=5}}; before {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} with an infinitive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=56|verse=10}}, and again before {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} with a suffix, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=64|verse=3|hidebook=1}};<ref>These are to be distinguished from the cases where {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} follows a construct state, which in conjunction with {{GHGheb|text=מִן}} (and the following {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}) has become a sort of preposition or adverb of place; thus, we have {{GHGheb|text=מִבֵּית־לְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=26|verse=33}} (for which in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=1|verse=27}} merely {{GHGheb|text=בֵּית לְ}}) meaning simply ''within''; {{GHGheb|text=מִימִין לְ}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=23|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=10|verse=3}}) ''on the right hand'' (i.e. south) ''of''; {{GHGheb|text=מִצְּפוֹן לְ}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=8|verse=11}}, 13, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=2|verse=9}}) ''on the north of''; cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=15|verse=21}} and {{GHGheb|text=לִפְנֵי מִן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=13|verse=4}}.</ref>—before {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=17}}; —before {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־}} (''with''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=6}}; —before {{GHGheb|text=מִן}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=9}} (a participle); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=13|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=7|verse=5}}; —before {{GHGheb|text=עַל־}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=10}}; —before {{GHGheb|text=בִּלְתִּי}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=6}}; —before the ''nota accus''. {{GHGheb|text=את}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=33|verse=22}}; —before a locative (which in such cases also serves as a genitive), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=27|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=1|verse=15}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|130|b}}
(2) Before ''wāw; copulative'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=26|verse=10}}; but {{GHGheb|text=חָכְמַת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=6}}, {{GHGheb|text=גִּילַת}} 35:2, and {{GHGheb|text=שְׁכֻרַת}} 51:21 may be cases of an intentional reversion to the old feminine ending ''ath'', in order to avoid the hiatus ({{GHGheb|text=וָ}}){{GHGheb|text=־ָה וְ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|130|c}}
(3) When it governs the (originally demonstrative) pronoun {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}}; so especially in the combination {{GHGheb|text=מְקוֹם אֲשֶׁר}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=40|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, ''the place where'' (prop. ''of that in which'') ''Joseph was bound''; cf. {{GHGpar|138|g}}; or {{GHGheb|text=בִּמְקוֹם אֲשֶׁר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=4|verse=24}}, 33, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=35}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=2|verse=1}}. We should expect {{GHGheb|text=הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר}}, {{GHGheb|text=בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר}}, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=35|verse=13}}, &c., ''at the place which...'', cf. § 138; but {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} is treated as a nomen rectum instead of as an attribute.<section end=par130 /><noinclude>
